head: DistroKid Publishing: royalties for songwriters, with Kobalt
dek: DistroKid has opened DistroKid Publishing, run with the music publisher Kobalt, to collect the songwriting royalties independent artists often miss. It costs a one-time 75 dollars, and songwriters keep 80% of what it collects.
details: You qualify with at least one release on DistroKid and more than 50 dollars in streaming revenue over the last 12 months. Original songs count, co-writes included, even if you own only a share; covers, remixes, mash-ups and fully AI-generated tracks don't. It collects mechanical and performance royalties, paid into your DistroKid Bank account: the first payment comes about six to nine months after your publishing earnings pass 10 dollars, then every quarter. There's no long-term commitment and you can leave at any time.
where: DistroKid members who meet the requirements, through the DistroKid dashboard
means: If you release your own songs through DistroKid and earn more than 50 dollars a year from streams, you can have your publishing royalties collected without signing with a publisher.
todo: Look for DistroKid Publishing in your DistroKid dashboard. Before you pay the 75 dollar fee, check which of your songs qualify: covers and remixes are left out.
